header:
Date: 2025-06-24
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (Synthetix Labs), Maya Chen (Synthetix Labs), Evan Park (Synthetix Labs)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review SDK integration, function/tool calling behavior, structured output formatting, and outstanding security questions. Focus on resolving a schema validation mismatch in structured responses and reviewing perf numbers for batching vs single-shot calls. Agreed next steps include sharing integration snippets, benchmark spreadsheet, and scheduling an in-env run with a 2GB sample dataset.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Tom Alvarez: Tom here, Maya, Evan.
[00:08] Maya Chen: Maya on the call.
[00:10] Evan Park: Evan as well.
[00:12] Jordan Lee: Great. Priya is on from our SE team, she'll lead the SDK/structured output deep dive.
[00:20] Priya Nambiar: Hey all, yeah hi. So last week we shipped the SDK snippet and you ran initial integration, I know there was a structured output mismatch where the app expected a 'steps' array and the model returned 'step_list' sometimes, could you confirm?
[00:35] Maya Chen: Yeah, exactly. The SDK wrapper seems to map function call name to a slightly different key when the model uses tool-calls vs function-calls, which I think is a transcriber, I mean a transformer behavior, uh on our end it's breaking the downstream parser.
[00:51] Tom Alvarez: To add, latency was fine overall but when we batched user prompts we saw unpredictable ordering of tool calls on a small percent of messages.
[01:03] Priya Nambiar: Okay, that's super helpful. A couple of things to flag: 1) SDK versions — make sure you're on redwood-js v0.9.2, the earlier patch had a rename bug; 2) function/tool calling differences can surface when the model falls back to a different variant (e.g., smaller quantized model) under load. We can force the same model variant in the pilot to avoid that flakey behavior.
[01:25] Evan Park: How do we pin the variant in the SDK?
[01:27] Priya Nambiar: You can set model: "redwood-rlhf-v1" and add variant: "fp16" in the request options; SDK will respect routing policy if the account allows pinned variants. I'll paste a snippet after this call.
[01:38] Jordan Lee: Priya also mentioned earlier there's a fix for the key rename - upgrading to 0.9.2 normalizes function output keys to the schema.
[01:45] Maya Chen: We saw two things in logs: the response object had both 'steps' and 'step_list' in rare cases, maybe partial decoding? Also our consumer app expects a strict JSON schema validated by AJV which fails if unknown keys are present.
[02:00] Priya Nambiar: Right. We recommend using the SDK's structuredOutput option which enforces a canonical JSON schema via the runtime's structured output mode. That will wrap the model response and validate it server-side, returning a canonical payload or an explicit parse error instead of a slightly different key name.
[02:18] Tom Alvarez: Is there a perf cost for structuredOutput? We care about latency at 95th pct.
[02:25] Priya Nambiar: Minimal. There's a tiny additional processing step for validation — usually 5-15ms on top of model latency. The bigger factors are batching and KV cache hits. If you enable structured mode plus caching, you get consistent payloads and lower token cost long term.
[02:40] Evan Park: On caching — we saw about 12% token reduction in initial tests, but when we increased batch size to 8 the p95 jumped ~120ms which is concerning.
[02:52] Priya Nambiar: That's the classic latency vs cost tradeoff. Batching increases throughput and lowers unit cost but can add tail latency. For interactive features we suggest batch sizes 2-4 and a latency SLO in routing policy. For high throughput background jobs you can batch more aggressively.
[03:10] Maya Chen: Could Redwood Dedicated help here? We need more predictable p95 if we commit.
[03:15] Jordan Lee: Yes Dedicated will give you reserved GPU pools and more consistent p95s; we can share a NUMs-per-hour baseline from other customers. I'll include pricing and the pilot SOW in the follow-up.
[03:26] Tom Alvarez: Sounds good. Back on structured output, can we see an example payload that Priya mentioned?
[03:30] Priya Nambiar: Sure — quick rough example: {"tool_calls": [{"name": "lookup_user", "args": {"user_id": "123"}}], "structured": {"steps": [{"id": 1, "text": "..."}]}}. The SDK structuredOutput option forces the model to emit that outer envelope and the runtime validates fields.
[03:50] Maya Chen: The issue is sometimes the model returns a top-level string instead of JSON when hallucinating — we need strict parse errors instead of silent fallback.
[03:58] Priya Nambiar: We can set strictParse: true which will return a parse_error event and also include the raw model text for debugging. That way your parser never gets malformed objects silently.
[04:10] Evan Park: Will that change token counts? If we get parse errors and have to re-run requests, cost could spike.
[04:16] Priya Nambiar: It could. For the POC, we recommend test runs with strictParse on in dev to catch edge cases, then for production you can use structured mode with fallback policies: on parse_error, do a single automatic retry with a different prompt template. The runtime supports that policy.
[04:33] Jordan Lee: Quick question from Tom — you mentioned ordering issues on batched tool calls. We should look at how you combine multiple user messages into batch payloads; if ordering is important, there's a per-request flag preserve_order: true.
[04:46] Tom Alvarez: We didn't find preserve_order in SDK docs, good to know. We'll add it.
[04:50] Maya Chen: Another nuance — our security team demands KMS-managed keys and audit logs for all requests. We need details on how Redwood's Private deployment handles key management and whether audit logs include per-token traces.
[05:02] Priya Nambiar: For Private and Dedicated you can integrate with your KMS/HSM; we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM via PKCS#11 for on-prem. Audit logs include per-request metadata (model, route, duration) and can be configured to include token-level cost breakdowns, but we do not log raw customer prompt content unless you enable that — by default prompts are not persisted for hosted mode. We'll send the security pack with SOC2 compliance details.
[05:26] Maya Chen: Great, please include specifics on encryption at rest and in transit and how key rotation is handled.
[05:31] Jordan Lee: Will do.
[05:33] Priya Nambiar: Back to integration — Maya, can you describe the exact validation failure? A snippet of the schema would help.
[05:38] Maya Chen: Yeah, we use AJV with schema: {type: "object", properties: {steps: {type: "array"}}, required: ["steps"]}. The response sometimes is {step_list: [...] } or {steps: null} when model says 'no steps'. AJV rejects both.
[05:54] Priya Nambiar: Two fixes: 1) upgrade SDK to 0.9.2 which ensures SDK normalizes tool outputs to 'steps' for the common adapters, and 2) enable structuredOutput+strictParse so you get a canonical envelope or a parse_error with reason.
[06:07] Tom Alvarez: Can you also confirm whether function calls vs tool calls appear differently in the webhook payload? We're sending the function outputs to our downstream processors via webhook.
[06:16] Priya Nambiar: Function vs tool call mapping is consistent in the latest runtime: both come through as call_type: "function" with a name field. The difference historically was in older SDKs where tool calls weren't normalized. This should be fixed by the upgrade.
[06:29] Evan Park: Good. On the SDK example we saw earlier, there was a small bug in the Node client where JSON.parse was wrapped in a try but swallowed the error and returned raw string.
[06:40] Priya Nambiar: Oh, we tracked that bug, it's in 0.9.1; 0.9.2 logs parse errors and surfaces them as parse_error events. That will help your telemetry.
[06:50] Maya Chen: For end-to-end testing, can Redwood host a small test environment with the same routing policies?
[06:56] Jordan Lee: Yes, we can provision a sandbox with pinned variants and the same routing rules. We'll need a point of contact and the dataset.
[07:04] Maya Chen: I'll share contact and dataset by EOD Friday.
[07:07] Tom Alvarez: On observability — are there per-route dashboards for structured output failures? We want to alert on parse_error counts.
[07:14] Priya Nambiar: Console exposes per-route error types including parse_error, token_overflow, model_fallback events. You can create alerts at a threshold. We'll attach a screenshot in the follow-up.
[07:25] Evan Park: A question about token accounting — our billing team wants clear per-call token breakdowns when batching. Does Redwood show per-user per-call token traces?
[07:34] Priya Nambiar: Yes, Console shows token-level breakdowns and you can get a raw CSV export with per-request tokens, prompt vs completion. When batching, the runtime attributes tokens to the originating request when preserve_order is set; otherwise attribution can be aggregated — depends on batch mode.
[07:50] Maya Chen: Okay that's helpful. Anything else on perf?
[07:54] Priya Nambiar: One tip: enable KV prefix caching for repeated prompts like 'system instructions' and static context; that reduces tokens and improves effective latency for subsequent calls. For interactive flows keep cache TTL short.
[08:06] Tom Alvarez: Can we do a quick check on the sample SDK snippet you promised?
[08:10] Priya Nambiar: Yep. Quick Node snippet: const res = await redwood.chat.create({model: 'redwood-rlhf-v1', variant: 'fp16', structuredOutput: true, strictParse: true, preserve_order: true, messages: [{role:'user', content:'Summarize steps for onboarding user 123'}]}); if (res.event === 'parse_error') { console.log('parse error', res.error); } else { const steps = res.structured.steps; }
[08:36] Evan Park: Nice. That maps to our consumer expecting res.structured.steps.
[08:40] Maya Chen: About per-request metadata — can we set a request_id and user_id so audit logs map to our systems?
[08:46] Priya Nambiar: Absolutely, pass metadata: {request_id: '...', user_id: '...'} in the options and it'll be included in logs and exported CSV. For Private deployments we can push logs to your SIEM via secure forwarder.
[08:58] Tom Alvarez: Security question about data residency — our customers in EU require data not leave region. Does Redwood support region pinning for hosted?
[09:06] Jordan Lee: Yes for hosted we have region pins and you can pin requests to EU regions. For strict residency we recommend Private deployment. We'll include region capabilities in the security pack.
[09:18] Maya Chen: Good. Anything else on the structured output schema?
[09:22] Priya Nambiar: One more recommendation: add a schema version in the envelope, e.g., structured: {schema_version: '1.0', steps: [...]}. That way you can evolve.
[09:32] Maya Chen: We'll do that.
[09:35] Jordan Lee: Alright let's do a quick recap and next steps. Priya?
[09:39] Priya Nambiar: Actions: I'll reproduce the schema mismatch locally, share a minimal repro and the SDK snippet, and confirm the upgrade path to 0.9.2. I'll also include the preserve_order usage and sample configs for batching/latency.
[09:52] Jordan Lee: I'll send pricing and Dedicated pilot SOW plus the security pack. We'll also provision a sandbox for the in-env run once we get the dataset from Maya.
[09:59] Maya Chen: I'll share dataset and contact by Friday and we plan to run the 2GB test week of 6/30.
[10:05] Tom Alvarez: I'll look at our alerting thresholds and prepare a small eval plan to measure p95 with batch sizes 1/2/4.
[10:12] Evan Park: And I'll validate the Node client parse errors and patch our wrapper accordingly.
[10:16] Jordan Lee: Great. Any final questions?
[10:18] Maya Chen: None from me.
[10:19] Tom Alvarez: All good.
[10:20] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and the spreadsheet.
[10:23] End of call.
